name: Muskingum University
academic_ranking: Private nonprofit liberal arts university founded in 1837 in New Concord, OH. Acceptance rate ~82% (test-optional admissions, accepts Common Application). Undergraduate enrollment roughly 1,400. Graduation rate ~57%. U.S. News/EDsmart place it in the mid-tier of national/regional institutions (EDsmart ~#691 nationally). Noted academic areas include liberal arts & social sciences, environmental science, and computer science.
financial_aid: Muskingum promotes itself as a strong value (ranked #1 Best Value among Ohio universities per its own site) and offers a Net Price Calculator. As an NCAA Division III program, no athletic scholarships are awarded; aid is merit- and need-based academic scholarships and grants. Reported average net tuition after aid is around $8,900. Figures vary by reporting year.
facilities_notes: Softball competes as part of Muskingum Athletics; coaching offices are located in the John Glenn Gymnasium complex (e.g., office 319C). Roster/facilities page hosted on fightingmuskies.com. Specific stadium/field details not confirmed from a live public page during 2026-07 check (athletics site blocked automated access).
program_reputation: Historically successful OAC program: the school cites 19 conference championships, 8 NCAA Regional Championships, and 1 National Championship. Recent success includes a 29-9 overall / 12-4 OAC season, a No. 2 OAC Tournament seed, multiple All-OAC honorees, and several Academic All-OAC honor roll selections. Picked third in a recent OAC Softball Preseason Poll.
notes: Researched 2026-07. The official athletics site (fightingmuskies.com; formerly muskies.muskingum.edu) blocks automated fetching (HTTP 403 / bot verification), so coaching-staff details were verified via the Muskingum University online directory (muskingum.edu/directory) and indexed search results of the official coaches page. Roster size could not be verified from a live public page (roster page blocked; search snippets were unreliable/conflicting), so roster_size is null rather than guessed. scholarship_count set to 0 because NCAA Division III programs do not offer athletic scholarships. Kylee Marcum was recently elevated from assistant to head coach.
